name: Airtable
api_surface: REST; 5 req/s per base, 50 req/s per personal access token; 429 then 30s lockout
embed: wrong_direction: Extensions/Blocks SDK renders inside Airtable's own UI; share-view iframes are read-only
license_state: SaaS ToS; Developer Terms 'Commercial Conduct' bars replicating or competing with Airtable core products, and bars sub-licensing API access to anyone without their own Airtable account
tenancy: per-end-user paid seat required; each User needs their own access token
verdict_reason: Developer Terms forbid using the API to replicate or compete with Airtable's core products; a table-backed app builder is that. Every end customer would also need their own paid account. 5 req/s per base is a hard per-app ceiling regardless.

name: Notion
api_surface: REST; pages, databases, data sources, views, comments, file uploads, search; webhooks present; ~3 req/s per connection average with bursts; 1000 blocks and 500KB max per request
embed: none: no embed SDK exists; official SDK is outbound only (our code calls Notion's REST API). Nothing renders Notion's editor inside a third-party app
license_state: UNVERIFIED - all terms URLs 307-redirect to app.notion.com which returns HTTP 401 or an empty body; 4 URL variants attempted
tenancy: workspace-scoped; per-workspace rate limit scales with plan
verdict_reason: No embed path in the inbound direction, so 'the app's docs ARE Notion pages' cannot be a block - only an outbound sync. Belongs to the Phase-8 connector lane. Terms unread but do not change this outcome.

name: Google Sheets
api_surface: REST; 300 read + 300 write requests/minute per project, 60/minute per user per project; free within quota, over-quota billing planned later in 2026
license_state: Google Workspace terms; not evaluated for resale since verdict rests on capability
tenancy: per-Google-account; quota is per-project and per-user
verdict_reason: A Sheet has no constraints, referential integrity, or row-level access model, so it is a liability as a generated app's data layer. Strong as an outbound connector, which is the other lane.

name: Coda
api_surface: REST at coda.io/apis/v1; reads 100 req/6s, writes 10 req/6s, doc-content writes 5 req/10s, listing docs 4 req/6s; no webhooks found, writes return 202 + requestId for polling
embed: none in the API reference; Packs run inside Coda
license_state: SaaS ToS; platform acquired and rebranded to Superhuman Docs mid-flight
verdict_reason: Tables are read-only via the API (list and get only, no create/update), so the builder cannot author a schema on it. Compounded by an in-flight rebrand under new ownership: coda.io/developers now 307-redirects to docs.superhuman.com.

name: SmartSuite
api_surface: REST covering Solutions, Tables, Records, Fields; rate limits UNVERIFIED, webhook status UNVERIFIED, API-access plan tier UNVERIFIED
embed: UNVERIFIED - no embed path surfaced on the developer site
verdict_reason: Rate limits, webhooks, plan-gating and embed are all unstated on the developer landing page. Smallest install base with the least published detail; nothing justifies the integration risk over Grist.

name: NocoDB
api_surface: REST; self-hostable Community edition, conditional webhooks included
embed: share-view embeds; not evaluated further because the licence gate fails first
license_state: Sustainable Use License v1.0 (LICENSE.md, updated 2026-01-29). Covers master and develop branches; other branches are NOT LICENSED AT ALL. Limitations clause: use or modify only for your own internal business purposes or non-commercial/personal use; may distribute or provide to others only free of charge for non-commercial purposes.
tenancy: multi-base on one instance, but moot under the licence
verdict_reason: Not open source despite being the highest-starred twin and marketed as 'Free Forever, Fair-Code' with no restriction stated on the pricing page. Commercial delivery of generated client apps is neither internal business purposes nor free-of-charge non-commercial distribution. CONTRACT.md rule 2 makes this AVOID, not STUDY.
evidence: gh api repos/nocodb/nocodb/contents/LICENSE.md (decoded body, Limitations section)

name: Baserow
api_surface: REST; JWT auth (60-minute tokens) plus scoped database tokens for safe data exposure; full OpenAPI spec at api.baserow.io/api/redoc/
embed: read_only: publicly shared views embed via iframe but grids are static and not clickable; only form views accept input. Hiding the Baserow logo is a paid feature.
license_state: MIT Expat core, plus proprietary premium/ and enterprise/ directories - BOTH VERIFIED PRESENT at root today. enterprise/LICENSE requires a valid paid Enterprise subscription for production use and forbids copy/merge/publish/distribute/sublicense/sell. All client-side JavaScript is MIT regardless. docs/ is CC BY-SA 4.0.
gate_scope: core only - premium/ and enterprise/ are AVOID
tenancy: multi-workspace on one instance via REST
verdict_reason: Best licence story after Grist and a real MIT core, but read-only embeds make it a headless data layer rather than a block. A generated app must write through the UI it embeds. Keep warm as the fallback.
evidence: gh api repos/bram2w/baserow/contents/ => premium and enterprise dirs both present

name: Grist
api_surface: REST over orgs, workspaces, docs, tables, columns and records; webhooks included in the free Community edition
embed: BOTH DIRECTIONS. Outbound: iframe embed of a Grist page, ?embed=true read-only or ?style=singlePage EDITABLE and following access rules. Inbound: grist-plugin-api.js custom widgets run our page inside a Grist doc.
license_state: Apache-2.0 at root, clean. NOTICE.txt carries no additional restriction. No gristlabs/grist-ee repo exists (HTTP 404). Community edition free to use and redistribute with NO licence key required; gristlabs/grist-oss image is purely free code. Paid full edition gates Admin Controls, email notifications, automations, AI assist and Azure snapshots - none load-bearing here.
tenancy: TRUE MULTI-TENANCY: one instance serves N orgs/team sites by leaving GRIST_SINGLE_ORG unset; access rules are per-table, per-row and per-column and are included free
verdict_reason: The only candidate clearing every gate: permissive licence we may host commercially for clients, genuine multi-tenancy on one instance, free access rules, and uniquely an EDITABLE embed that honours those rules. Absorbs the hard must-have data.query_and_mutation_model plus two moderate ones.
evidence: gh api repos/gristlabs/grist-ee => HTTP 404 Not Found

name: AppFlowy
api_surface: client is Flutter/Rust; server half is AppFlowy-Cloud (1996 stars, also AGPL-3.0)
embed: not evaluated - licence gate fails first
license_state: AGPL-3.0 verified in LICENSE body at root; companion server repo AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy-Cloud is also AGPL-3.0
tenancy: self-hostable but moot under the block contract
verdict_reason: AGPL-3.0. The block contract's provenance.license enum admits only MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/ISC/first-party, so no AGPL code may appear in a block. The network clause is the specific hazard: serving generated apps to clients from AGPL code triggers source-disclosure over the combined work. Architecture only.

name: Outline
embed: not evaluated - licence gate fails first
license_state: Business Source License 1.1, Licensor General Outline Inc, Licensed Work Outline 1.9.1. Additional Use Grant permits production use EXCEPT you may not use the Licensed Work for a 'Document Service', defined as a commercial offering letting third parties create teams and documents they control. Change Date 2030-07-13, Change License Apache-2.0. The licence text itself states BSL is not an Open Source licence.
verdict_reason: The BSL Additional Use Grant carve-out describes our use case almost exactly: generated client apps whose docs are Outline, with third parties controlling their own teams and documents, is a Document Service. Converts to Apache-2.0 on 2030-07-13, which is four years out and not a plan.
evidence: gh api repos/outline/outline/contents/LICENSE (decoded body, Parameters block with Additional Use Grant)

name: Docmost
embed: not evaluated - licence gate fails first
license_state: AGPL-3.0 core plus a PROPRIETARY ENTERPRISE EDITION split. README states files in apps/server/src/ee, apps/client/src/ee and packages/ee are under the Docmost Enterprise licence defined in packages/ee/License. The apps/server/src/ee directory was confirmed present.
tenancy: self-hostable but moot under the licence
verdict_reason: AGPL-3.0 core is inadmissible under the block contract's provenance licence enum, and an additional proprietary EE layer sits inside the same repo across three directories. Architecture only.
evidence: gh api repos/docmost/docmost/contents/LICENSE (decoded head, GNU AGPL v3)
gh api repos/docmost/docmost/contents/README.md (decoded tail, Enterprise licence directory list)

name: Teable
embed: not evaluated - licence gate fails first
license_state: SPLIT. LICENSE body: core applications apps/nestjs-backend and apps/nextjs-app are AGPL-3.0; everything under packages/ is MIT. Project is stated to be 'primarily under the AGPL-3.0 license'. Additional Section 7(e) brand-protection terms forbid modifying, replacing or removing Teable brand assets.
gate_scope: packages/ only is MIT; both applications are AGPL
tenancy: self-hostable but moot for the application code
verdict_reason: The MIT half is SDK and utility scaffolding; the two directories that constitute the actual product are AGPL-3.0. The Section 7(e) brand-protection terms also block the logo removal that white-labelled client delivery requires. Architecture only.
evidence: gh api repos/teableio/teable/contents/LICENSE (decoded body, licensing split plus Section 7(e) brand protection)
